result.title: DeliverBench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Delivering Realistic Multi-Stage Professional Projects
result.summary: LLM agents are judged by what they deliver, and in professional work what gets delivered is a project, not a task. A project pays off only if the whole package holds, and one weak part can limit the value of the rest. Yet existing benchmarks mostly test agents on one task at a time, leaving a gap between the capability we measure and the outcome that makes agents useful. To address this gap, we introduce DeliverBench, which tests whether agents can carry a project from brief to final delivery. Its 11 projects, spanning financial due diligence, legal contract drafting, and drug safety reporting, are reconstructed with 13 domain experts from real materials and chain 150 subtasks through 2-15 rounds of new materials and client feedback. Because no reference outputs are injected, agents inherit their own errors from one task to the next. Expert rubrics then score every checkpoint as well as the final package. Across seven model-harness systems, even the best system scores only 65.0 out of 100 on final delivery and passes 50.0% of subtasks at a 90-point threshold. The failures are often failures of carrying work forward: in one audit project, all seven systems addressed the review findings, but only one preserved traceability. Together, these results suggest that task-level capability does not simply compose into delivery, which also depends on keeping the work coherent as it evolves.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 DeliverBench，用 11 个由领域专家重构的专业项目（尽调、合同起草、药物安全报告）把 150 个子任务串联成 2–15 轮、带回填材料与客户反馈的长链条，且不注入参考输出，由专家 rubric 对每个检查点和最终交付评分；七个模型-框架组合中最好的最终交付仅 65.0 分。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽无视觉与 latent 推理要素，但其「错误跨步继承」「工作能否连贯前推」的失败模式，可能启发 LVR 中长程推理状态的保持、错误累积与贡献分配的评测设计，可供核查。
